Professional fashion photograph, full body shot. ONE woman standing.

a luminous warm-ivory complexion, early 30s goddess, glamour hourglass physique THE MOST EXTREME PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE beyond all anatomy limits — a stunning hourglass figure, far more dramatically curved than any ordinary woman; a full, rounded bust, a dramatically narrow, sharply cinched waist with a deep shadowed groove running around her middle, and wide, curvaceous hips flaring well beyond her shoulders, soft rounded thighs, toned but soft arms; her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other, wolf cut honey blonde hair — her body is painted in 4 different painting styles at once, each style claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 wedge-shaped regions radiating from a single centre point located about 55% of the way down her figure from the top on the centre line of her figure. 4 hazy ray-shaped transition zones leave that centre pointing toward 10 o'clock, 12 o'clock, 5 o'clock and 8 o'clock as seen by the camera, where 12 o'clock points straight up. Region 1 is the wedge between the 10 o'clock ray and the 12 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it carries Mondrian style grid of thick black lines with flat blocks of primary red, yellow and blue and white. Region 2 is the wedge between the 12 o'clock ray and the 5 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it carries Van Gogh Starry Night style swirling thick brushstrokes in deep ultramarine, cobalt and glowing yellow, big spiralling skies flowing over her curves. Region 3 is the wedge between the 5 o'clock ray and the 8 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it carries Mucha style Art Nouveau flowing floral curves with soft pastel flowers and ornamental whiplash lines. Region 4 is the wedge between the 8 o'clock ray and the 10 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it carries Miro style playful biomorphic shapes, stars and curling black lines on flat primary colour fields. Where two regions meet, the two neighbouring paintings blend along the edge: brushwork of one reaches into the other and the two styles simply touch, so the boundary is made only of the two neighbouring paintings, with no gap between them. Each transition zone follows a smooth, even, straight course, every painting laid on her own living skin and covering her completely from neck to ankle. Her face and ears stay real living skin with visible pores, fine peach-fuzz hairs and a soft natural flush. Pose: standing facing the camera straight on, her left hand resting on her hip and her right arm relaxed at her side, her legs fully in view — most extreme glamour hourglass silhouette ever displayed.

Jewelry: a pair of large hoop earrings of polished gold with blackened iron accents as her only jewelry, her neck, collarbones, chest, arms, wrists and fingers plain bare skin.

Skin: the skin of a real living woman photographed with a macro lens at close range, every area of her body showing real pores, fine vellus hairs catching the light, a natural soft sheen of skin oils, subtle natural freckles and small beauty marks scattered across her shoulders, arms, stomach and thighs, a gentle uneven skin tone with a faint blush at the knees and elbows, and a soft warm translucency where the light passes through her skin, sharp enough to read every skin texture detail. Her skin shows satin skin finish, smooth silky sheen.

Background: the sunlit arches of the Roman Colosseum with worn stone paving, standard-height arched doorways and low stone steps, empty of tourists, in clear sunny daylight, lit by natural light with soft shadows, the whole floor and surroundings clearly visible and in focus. ONE woman only. Full-length wide shot from a moderate distance with the camera at waist height, the whole figure from the soles of her shoes to the top of her head completely visible, with the door, railing or steps beside her at normal human scale so the extreme heel height reads at a glance, the towering heels clearly separating the shoes from the floor.
